The original equation requires a≠b, and the displayed solved form additionally requires m+ca≠0.
The original equation does not guarantee m+ca≠0. If m+ca=0 and the original equation is solvable, then m=0 and ca=0; every b≠a satisfies it, so b is not uniquely determined.
D is the intended explicit isolated form. A and B are also rearranged identities wherever their denominators are nonzero, but retain b on the right-hand side.
